name: Single Variable Calculus
about: Limits, derivatives and integrals of functions of one variable, and the series that build them.

name: Multivariable Calculus
about: Vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and calculus on curves and surfaces.

name: Introduction to EECS I
about: Programs, state machines, signals and systems, circuits, and estimating state from noisy evidence.

name: Differential Equations
about: Equations about rates of change: first and second order, oscillators, Laplace transforms and systems.

name: Introduction to EECS II
about: Digital communication: noise, error-correcting codes, modulation, and packet networks.

name: Mathematics for Computer Science
about: Proofs, induction, graphs, counting and discrete probability.

name: Introduction to Algorithms
about: Sorting, hashing, search trees, graph search, shortest paths and dynamic programming.

name: Linear Algebra
about: Systems of linear equations, the four subspaces of a matrix, orthogonality, determinants, eigenvalues and the singular value decomposition.

name: Probabilistic Systems Analysis
about: Probability models, random variables, limit theorems, Markov chains and inference.

name: Circuits and Electronics
about: Circuit laws, the digital abstraction, transistors, energy storage, filters and operational amplifiers.

name: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
about: Divide and conquer, randomization, amortization, network flow, approximation and complexity.

name: Artificial Intelligence
about: Search, games, constraints, and learning from examples: trees, neighbors, neural networks and boosting.

name: Signals and Systems
about: Linear time-invariant systems, feedback, and the Laplace, Z and Fourier transforms.

name: Computation Structures
about: How a computer is built: information, logic gates, sequential logic, processors, pipelines and memory.

name: Logic I
about: Truth-functional and first-order logic: what follows from what, and how to prove it.

name: Computer System Engineering
about: Naming, modularity, performance, networks, reliability, atomicity and security in large systems.

name: Logic II
about: Logic about logic: completeness, computability, and Gödel's incompleteness theorems.

name: Communication, Control and Signal Processing
about: State-space models, random signals, and estimation and detection in noise.

name: Elements of Software Construction
about: State machines, grammars, abstract data types, invariants and concurrency, for software that is correct and stays so.

name: Machine Vision
about: How images form, and how to recover shape, motion and position from them.

name: Computer Graphics
about: Ray tracing, transformations, curves and surfaces, animation, shading and the graphics pipeline.

name: Theory of Computation
about: Automata, grammars, Turing machines, decidability and complexity.
